item.title: Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson wins Nobel Prize in literature
item.description:
Anne Carson, who won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature today, doesn’t write masterpieces or door-stoppers, and she has no interest in emulating the great works of the past—including those of past laureates. Despite her training as a classicist and her celebrated skill as a translator, she would likely have little to say about the authenticity of film adaptations of The Odyssey . Carson is a poet by trade, but she’s really an archaeologist of sorts, sifting through the pottery shards of culture and letting the light of our own time illuminate their beauty. Carson prefers to use fragments as seeds for her own poetry, and the high-cultural touchpoints for her lyrics and critical essays—Sappho, Samuel Beckett, Franz Kafka, Michelangelo Antonioni, Simone Weil—sometimes give her work an air of forbidding experimentation that quickly turns, upon reading, into pleasure and delight. item.title: ‘Nothing will stop us’: French student protests show few signs of ending
item.description:
Schools blockaded again across country as teenagers and teachers demand more investment and ‘concrete measures’ to improve conditions High school students have again blockaded schools and marched through cities across France, promising to continue their campaign despite government pledges to address the grievances underlying 10 days of protests that have left hundreds injured. Large crowds took to the streets on Thursday for mainly peaceful demonstrations in cities including Lille, Rennes, Nantes, Lyon, Toulon and Marseille, while in Paris a large procession marched through the city centre to the Place de la Bastille. item.title: Israel shuts down British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem
item.description:
UK and Israel back away from full diplomatic confrontation, though British presence in Palestine will be much reduced UK politics live – latest updates Israel and the UK have backed away from a full-scale diplomatic confrontation, with Britain announcing it is rebranding its consulate general ⁠building in ⁠East Jerusalem as a UK mission, a move that will result in UK diplomats leaving Israel, with only seven to remain in the building. Among those leaving is the consul general, Helen Winterton. The change was forced on the UK by the Israeli government as punishment for the decision by the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, last month to ban trade with illegal settlements and introduce a tougher sanctions regime against those who aided the building of settlements. The UK is seeking to protect the two-state solution as the best means of ending the Israel-Palestine conflict. Continue reading...
